lead.headline: Arcade Alley widens the lane for computer games
lead.dek: Video magazine coverage treats Apple II and home-computer games as part of the same conversation as Zaxxon and Turbo.
lead.body: In the spring 1983 game press, the wall between coin-op excitement and personal-computer software kept getting thinner. Electronic Games expanded its Arcade Alley column to cover computer gaming, reviewing Zaxxon, Turbo, and Apple II titles in the same breath. For shoppers with an Apple II, Atari 8-bit, Commodore 64, or VIC-20, that mattered: game disks were no longer just hobby curiosities, but a front-counter reason to compare graphics, joysticks, and disk drives.
lead.confidence: High for the April 1983 Arcade Alley coverage; medium for week-specific retail emphasis.

Antic Vol. 2 No. 4 listed products including KoalaPad and Knights of the Desert.
Lotus 1-2-3 was released in 1983 and became a defining IBM PC business application.
